86	\section{The source calculation}
    87	
    88	Natarajan and Vidick define the distance between two POVMs by summing the
    89	squared state-dependent distances between corresponding square roots
    90	\cite[Section~3.1]{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  For projective measurements the
    91	square roots are the effects themselves.  In the binary case their calculation
    92	expands $P_S^\pm=(\Id\pm S)/2$ and obtains
    93	\[
    94	  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2
    95	    = 1-\frac12\tr_\rho(ST+TS)
    96	    = \frac12\tr_\rho((S-T)^2).
    97	  \tag{source equation (3)}
    98	\]
    99	This is equation~(3) at lines~903--910 of the in-repository source mirror.%
   100	\footnote{See
   101	\path{references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex}, lines~866--912.  The quantum
   102	linearity theorem and its Fourier--Naimark proof are at lines~1074--1112.}
   103	The next line identifies the final expression with the squared state-dependent
   104	operator distance.  The operator-distance definition at lines~873--875 is
   105	printed with $\rho$ occurring twice,
   106	\[
   107	  d_\rho(S,T)^2 = \tr_\rho\big((S-T)^\dagger(S-T)\rho\big),
   108	  \qquad \tr_\rho(X) := \tr(\rho X),
   109	\]
   110	and we read the duplication as typographical, keeping the single $\rho$ of the
   111	definition of $d$ above.  Under that reading the squared state-dependent
   112	operator distance is $\tr_\rho((S-T)^2)$ rather than one half of that
   113	quantity.  Thus the calculation through line~910 is correct and the equality
   114	on line~911 loses a factor of two.
   115	
   116	The Fourier--Naimark proof is consistent with the measurement normalization.
   117	It proves
   118	\[
   119	  \mathbb E_a\operatorname{CON}_{\rho'}(A(a),\mathcal A(a))
   120	  = \frac12+\frac12\mathbb E_{a,b}
   121	       \tr_\rho(A(a)A(b)A(a+b)).
   122	\]
   123	The hypothesis therefore makes the consistency deficit at most $\delta/2$.
   124	For binary projective measurements, the squared measurement distance is twice
   125	that deficit, giving the bound $\delta$ for the squared binary-measurement
   126	distance and the bound $2\delta$ for the squared state-dependent operator
   127	distance.
   128	
   129	\section{A four-point counterexample}
   130	
   131	The bound $\delta$ for the mean squared state-dependent operator distance is
   132	false.  Let $G=(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^2$, choose $r\in G\setminus\{0\}$, take
   133	the one-dimensional state $\rho=1$, and define scalar binary observables by
   134	\[
   135	  A(a)=\begin{cases}
   136	    -1,&a=r,\\
   137	     1,&a\neq r.
   138	  \end{cases}
   139	\]
   140	For the characters $\chi_u(a)=(-1)^{u\cdot a}$, the normalized Fourier
   141	coefficients satisfy
   142	\[
   143	  \widehat A(0)=\frac12,
   144	  \qquad
   145	  \widehat A(u)=-\frac12\chi_u(r)\quad(u\neq0).
   146	\]
   147	Their multiset is
   148	$\{\frac12,\frac12,\frac12,-\frac12\}$, and hence
   149	\[
   150	  \mathbb E_{a,b}A(a)A(b)A(a+b)
   151	    =\sum_u\widehat A(u)^3=\frac14.
   152	\]
   153	The correlation hypothesis therefore holds with $\delta=3/4$.
   154	
   155	Every scalar exact Boolean representation is one of the characters $\chi_u$,
   156	and its mean squared state-dependent operator distance from $A$ is
   157	\[
   158	  \mathbb E_a |A(a)-\chi_u(a)|^2
   159	    =2-2\widehat A(u)\geq1.
   160	\]
   161	Allowing an ancillary space does not reduce this lower bound.  Exact linearity
   162	and the binary-observable relations make the operators $\mathcal A(a)$ a
   163	commuting family of Hermitian involutions.  Their simultaneous spectral
   164	subspaces carry characters of $G$.  Evaluation in any density operator is
   165	therefore a convex combination of the scalar character correlations above, so
   166	the mean squared state-dependent operator distance remains at least $1$.  It
   167	cannot be at most $\delta=3/4$.  By~\eqref{eq:normalization}, the corresponding
   168	mean squared binary-measurement distance has lower bound $1/2$, which is
   169	compatible with the provider's conclusion.
   170	
   171	\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
   172	
   173	The QPBT paper quotes the quantum linearity theorem at lines~711--725 of its
   174	Pauli-basis analysis and defers its proof to Natarajan and Vidick.%
   175	\footnote{See
   176	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   177	lines~711--725.}
   178	The active blueprint expands the conclusion's distance as the state-dependent
   179	operator distance $d$ while retaining the bound $\delta$.  The formal theorem
   180	\leanid{exists\_exactly\_linear\_observables}, whose conclusion bounds the
   181	average over $u$ of \leanid{stateDepDistSq} by $\delta$, makes the same
   182	choice.  Thus both carry the false normalization exhibited by the
   183	counterexample.%
   184	\footnote{See
   185	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex}, lines~124--132, and
   186	\leanid{exists\_exactly\_linear\_observables} together with
   187	\leanid{stateDepDistSq} in
   188	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean}.}
   189	
   190	The mathematical content of the theorem is nevertheless available in the
   191	correct normalization.  The stability theorem
   192	\leanid{exists\_exact\_boolean\_representation} assumes the mean squared
   193	state-dependent multiplicative defect
   194	\[
   195	  \mathbb E_{a,b}\, d_\rho\big(A(a)A(b), A(a+b)\big)^2 \le \eta
   196	\]
   197	and produces an ancillary space, a unit vector $\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$ in it and
   198	an exactly linear family $\{\mathcal A(a)\}$ of binary observables with
   199	$\mathbb E_a\, d_{\rho'}(\mathcal A(a), A(a)\otimes\Id)^2 \le \eta$, where
   200	$\rho' = \rho \otimes \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}$.
   201	Its bound rests on an identity rather than an inequality:
   202	\leanid{avg\_stateDepDistSq\_roundedObservable\_eq\_avg\_multiplicativeDefect}
   203	proves that the two averages above coincide, both being $2-2C$ for the
   204	two-query correlation
   205	$C = \mathbb E_{a,b}\Re\tr(A(a)A(b)A(a+b)\rho)$ of the linearity test.%
   206	\footnote{Both declarations are in
   207	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/Stability.lean}; the blueprint
   208	records them as \texttt{lem:boolean-representation-stability}.}
   209	The source hypothesis $C \ge 1-\delta$ is therefore exactly the hypothesis of
   210	the stability theorem with $\eta = 2\delta$, and the theorem then yields the
   211	mean squared state-dependent operator distance bound $2\delta$: the corrected
   212	conclusion identified above, with no restriction on $\delta$ and no commutation
   213	assumption on the $A(a)$.  This reparameterization is the entire
   214	content of the repair, so the corrected source-facing statement is obtained
   215	from \leanid{exists\_exact\_boolean\_representation} by substituting
   216	$\eta = 2\delta$.
   217	
   218	The Boolean Fourier foundation keeps the state-dependent operator distance
   219	unchanged and adds the separately named binary-measurement distance together
   220	with equations~\eqref{eq:normalization}--\eqref{eq:binary-correlation}.  It
   221	does not advertise the current source-labelled theorem as proved.  The
   222	statement repair should change the conclusion either to mean squared
   223	binary-measurement distance at most $\delta$ or to mean squared
   224	state-dependent operator distance at most $2\delta$, deriving the latter from
   225	the stability theorem by the reparameterization just described, and
   226	synchronize the blueprint at the same time.%
   227	\footnote{The normalization investigation is tracked in
   228	\ghissue{124}; the source-facing statement repair is assigned to
   229	\ghissue{129}.}
   230	
   231	\section{Conclusion}
   232	
   233	The provider's binary-measurement calculation is correct through the factor
   234	$1/2$ in equation~(3), but its final identification with the squared
   235	state-dependent operator distance is incorrect.  The theorem proved by the
   236	Fourier--Naimark argument has mean squared binary-measurement error at most
   237	$\delta$, equivalently mean squared state-dependent operator error at most
   238	$2\delta$.  The four-point example rules out the current bound $\delta$ for the
   239	mean squared state-dependent operator distance even when arbitrary ancillary
   240	extensions are allowed.

   927	\begin{proof}
   928	The proof of both results is identical, and uses the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality;
   929	we show only the proof of the second. Let $A^a = \sqrt{M^a}$ and $B^a = \sqrt{N^a}$. Applying the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality,
   930	  \begin{align*}

   937	A second measure of proximity that is often convenient is the
   938	\emph{consistency}. As before, let $\{M^a\}$ and $\{N^a\}$ be POVMs
   939	with the same number of outcomes. Then their consistency is defined
   940	as
   941	\[ \CON_\rho(M, N) = \Re \Big(\sum_a \Trho\big( M^a N^a \big)\Big), \]
   942	so that by~\eqref{eq:dpsi-1a} we have 
   943	\begin{equation} \label{eq:condist}\Drho(\sqrt{M}, \sqrt{N})^2 = 2-2
   944	\CON_\rho(\sqrt{M},\sqrt{N}).\end{equation}
   945	 For collections of binary observables $\{A(a)\}$ and $\{B(a)\}$ we use
   946	\begin{align*}
   947	 \CON_\rho(A,B) &= \sum_a \Re \Big( \sum_{c\in\{0,1\}} \frac{1}{4} \Trho \big( (\Id+(-1)^cA(a))(\Id+(-1)^c B(a) )\big)\Big)\\

   966	Given two observables $A$ and $B$, the product $AB$ is an observable
   967	if and only if $A$ and $B$ commute. The following lemma shows how to define
   968	a ``product'' observable $C$ when $A$ and $B$ commute only
   969	approximately in state-dependent distance, such that the action of $C$
   970	on the state is close to $AB$ (and $BA$).
   971	\begin{lemma}
   972	  Let $\rho$ be a density matrix and $A, B$ observables such that
   973	  $\Drho(AB,BA) \leq \delta$ for some $\delta\geq 0$. Let $C$ be the observable defined by
   974	  \[ C = \frac{AB + BA}{|AB + BA|} , \]
   975		 where we use the convention
   976	  that $M/ |M|$ is defined as the identity on the kernel of $M$. Then
   977	  $$\max\Big\{ \Drho(C,AB),\,\Drho(C,BA)\Big\}\, \leq\, \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\delta.$$
   978	  \label{lem:jointobs}
   979	\end{lemma}
   980	
   981	\begin{proof}
   982	  It is clear from the definition that $C$ is Hermitian and an
   983	  observable (i.e. all its eigenvalues are $\pm 1$). Evaluate
   984	  \begin{align*}
   985	   \Drho(AB, C)^2 &=  2 - \Trho\Big( \frac{AB + BA}{|AB + BA|} AB + BA \frac{AB

   987				\end{align*}
   988	 Notice that $AB$ and $BA$ both commute with $(AB + BA)$ and
   989	  hence with $(AB + BA)/|AB + BA|$. Thus the above
   990	    expression simplifies to

   994	    &\leq 2 - \frac{1}{2} \Trho\big( (AB + BA)^2 \big) \\

     4	/-!
     5	# The quantum linearity theorem
     6	
     7	This file states the external quantum-linearity result used to combine the
     8	binary observables produced in the point analysis.  The statement uses a
     9	positive semidefinite trace-one operator, and its conclusion adjoins a finite ancillary
    10	space on which the exactly linear observables act.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The declaration is `thm:linearity` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`.  The quotation in the
    16	QPBT paper is at
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`; the
    18	provider is Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- A binary observable is a Hermitian operator whose square is the identity.
    31	This is the finite-matrix realization of `Obs(H)` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    32	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`, quoted at paper
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`. -/
    34	def IsBinaryObservable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    35	    (O : Op ι) : Prop :=
    36	  O.IsHermitian ∧ O * O = 1
    37	
    38	/-- The rank-one density operator associated with an ancillary vector. -/
    39	noncomputable def ancProj {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    40	    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : Op ι :=
    41	  let w := (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ) v
    42	  Matrix.vecMulVec w (star w)
    43	
    44	/-- Squared state-dependent distance between two operators.  This is the
    45	quantity `d_rho(S,T)^2` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`. -/
    47	noncomputable def stateDepDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    48	    (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    49	  (Matrix.trace ((S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) * ρ)).re
    50	
    51	/-- The quantum linearity theorem imported from Natarajan--Vidick.
    52	
    53	The statement is `thm:linearity` in
    54	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-145`; the QPBT paper quotes
    55	it at
    56	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`.
    57	
    58	As recorded in `rem:linearity-import` (blueprint lines 147--180), this
    59	provider-faithful form imposes no upper bound on `δ`, preserves the error,
    60	asserts exact linearity for every pair, and averages closeness only over `u`.
    61	The paper quotation instead adds `δ ≤ 1`, phrases closeness pointwise under a
    62	pair quantifier, and appends `L 0 = 1`; those three deviations are not
    63	reproduced.  The identity at zero follows later from exact linearity and the
    64	binary-observable condition. -/
    65	theorem exists_exactly_linear_observables {ι : Type}
    66	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    67	    (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    68	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
    69	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι)
    70	    (hO : ∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (O u))
    71	    (hcorrelation :
    72	      1 - δ ≤ avgOver
    73	        (uniformDistribution
    74	          ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
    75	        (fun pair =>
    76	          (Matrix.trace
    77	            (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)) :
    78	    ∃ (ι' : Type) (_ : Fintype ι') (_ : DecidableEq ι')
    79	        (anc : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι'),
    80	      ‖anc‖ = 1 ∧
    81	        ∃ L : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op (ι × ι'),
    82	          (∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (L u)) ∧
    83	          (∀ u u', L u * L u' = L (u + u')) ∧
    84	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
    85	              (fun u => stateDepDistSq (L u)
    86	                (heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op ι'))
    87	                (heteroKron ρ (ancProj anc))) ≤ δ := by
    88	  sorry
    89	
    90	end
    91

    54	/-! ## The two-query correlation and the multiplicative defect -/
    55	
    56	/-- The two-query correlation of the linearity test: the average, over a
    57	uniformly random pair `(u, u')` in `𝔽_2^t`, of the real part of
    58	`Tr(O^u O^{u'} O^{u+u'} ρ)`.  This is the left-hand side of display (7) in
    59	Natarajan--Vidick, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`, and the
    60	quantity bounded below in the hypothesis of
    61	`exists_exactly_linear_observables`; the order of the two uniform variables is
    62	the one used there. -/
    63	def blrCorrelation {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    64	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    65	  avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
    66	    (fun pair =>
    67	      (Matrix.trace (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)
    68	
    69	/-- The state-dependent squared defect of the product `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}`,
    70	namely `d_ρ(O^u O^v, O^{u+v})^2` for the state-dependent distance of
    71	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:873-875`.  Its average over uniformly random
    72	`u, v` is the approximate-linearity error of the family in the sense of the QPBT
    73	quotation `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`,
    74	measured with the squared state-dependent operator distance
    75	`stateDepDistSq`. -/
    76	def multiplicativeDefect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    77	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℝ :=
    78	  stateDepDistSq (O u * O v) (O (u + v)) ρ
    79	
    80	/-- Pointwise form of the defect identity: for binary observables the squared
    81	defect of `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}` is `2 - 2 Re Tr(O^v O^u O^{v+u} ρ)`.  The
    82	expansion of `(O^u O^v - O^{u+v})^† (O^u O^v - O^{u+v})` produces the two
    83	triple products `O^v O^u O^{u+v}` and `O^{u+v} O^u O^v`; the second is the
    84	adjoint of the first, so their traces against `ρ` are complex conjugates with
    85	equal real parts.  This is the calculation behind display (3) of
    86	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`, applied to the products of the
    87	family. -/
    88	theorem multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
    89	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    90	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
    91	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
    92	    (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    93	    multiplicativeDefect O ρ u v =
    94	      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (v + u) * ρ)).re := by
    95	  have hu := hO u
    96	  have hv := hO v
    97	  have huv := hO (u + v)
    98	  have hdiff :
    99	      (O u * O v - O (u + v))ᴴ * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
   100	        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) - O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
   101	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq,
   102	      huv.1.eq]
   103	    calc
   104	      (O v * O u - O (u + v)) * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
   105	          O v * (O u * O u) * O v - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
   106	            O (u + v) * O u * O v + O (u + v) * O (u + v) := by
   107	        noncomm_ring
   108	      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
   109	            O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
   110	        rw [hu.2, Matrix.mul_one, hv.2, huv.2]
   111	        module
   112	  have hstar :
   113	      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
   114	        Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
   115	    calc
   116	      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
   117	          Matrix.trace ((O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)ᴴ) := by
   118	        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
   119	      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * (O v * O u * O (u + v))) := by
   120	        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq, huv.1.eq,
   121	          hρ.isHermitian.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc]
   122	      _ = Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
   123	        exact Matrix.trace_mul_comm _ _
   124	  have hcross :
   125	      (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)).re =
   126	        (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ)).re := by
   127	    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
   128	    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
   129	  unfold multiplicativeDefect stateDepDistSq
   130	  rw [hdiff]
   131	  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
   132	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
   133	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   134	  rw [hcross, add_comm v u]
   135	  ring

   141	exchanging the two coordinates leaves the average unchanged.  This is the
   142	relation between the approximate-linearity hypothesis of the QPBT quotation

   153	      2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   154	  have hswap :
   155	      avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))

   157	          (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) =
   158	        blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   159	    unfold blrCorrelation
   160	    refine (avgOver_uniform_equiv (Equiv.prodComm _ _) _).trans ?_
   161	    exact avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair => rfl)

   163	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))

   165	        avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))

   167	            (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) :=
   168	      avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair =>
   169	        multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace
   170	          pair.1 pair.2)
   171	    _ = 2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   172	      rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_mul, avgOver_uniform_const, hswap]

   313	/-! ## The Fourier-square POVM and its overlap certificate -/
   314	
   315	/-- Each Fourier square `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` of a Hermitian operator family is
   316	positive semidefinite, being the product of a Hermitian matrix with its
   317	adjoint.  This is the positivity half of the assertion that the `B^u` form a

+
+The provider's binary-measurement calculation is correct through the factor

+state-dependent operator distance is incorrect.  The theorem proved by the

+$\delta$, equivalently mean squared state-dependent operator error at most

+/-!
+# The operator-valued BLR bound
+
+This file carries out the Fourier-analytic part of the proof of the quantum
+linearity theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  Given binary observables `O^u`
+indexed by the Boolean cube `𝔽_2^t` and a positive semidefinite trace-one
+operator `ρ`, it expresses the state-dependent multiplicative defect of the
+family through the two-query correlation of the linearity test, identifies the
+sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients with that correlation, and records the
+overlap certificate for the Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` used in the
+Naimark-dilation argument.  Pairwise commutation of the observables is never
+assumed, and every complex trace is handled through its real part.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `multiplicativeDefect`: the state-dependent squared defect of `O^u O^v`
+  from `O^{u+v}`.
+* `avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` and
+  `avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`: the average defect equals
+  `2 - 2 * (correlation)`, hence is at most `2 * δ` under the correlation
+  hypothesis of `exists_exactly_linear_observables`.
+* `operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation`: the identity
+  `∑_u Tr_ρ((hat O^u)^3) = E_{a,b} Tr_ρ(O^a O^b O^{a+b})`.
+* `fourierSquareMeasurement` and `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`:
+  the Fourier-square POVM together with its overlap certificate.
+
+## References
+
+Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, Theorem 10 with displays (7)--(8) and
+its proof, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`; the state-dependent
+distance is defined at lines 866--900 of the same file.  The QPBT paper quotes
+the theorem at
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725` and
+invokes it at lines 787--832.  The blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:81-147`.  The normalization of
+the error constant is analyzed in
+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`: the exact defect
+bound is `2 * δ` for the squared state-dependent operator distance
+`stateDepDistSq`, equivalently `δ` for the squared binary-observable distance.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+

+/-! ## The two-query correlation and the multiplicative defect -/
+
+/-- The two-query correlation of the linearity test: the average, over a
+uniformly random pair `(u, u')` in `𝔽_2^t`, of the real part of
+`Tr(O^u O^{u'} O^{u+u'} ρ)`.  This is the left-hand side of display (7) in
+Natarajan--Vidick, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`, and the
+quantity bounded below in the hypothesis of
+`exists_exactly_linear_observables`; the order of the two uniform variables is
+the one used there. -/
+def blrCorrelation {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
+  avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
+    (fun pair =>
+      (Matrix.trace (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)
+
+/-- The state-dependent squared defect of the product `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}`,
+namely `d_ρ(O^u O^v, O^{u+v})^2` for the state-dependent distance of
+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:873-875`.  Its average over uniformly random
+`u, v` is the approximate-linearity error of the family in the sense of the QPBT
+quotation `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`,
+measured with the squared state-dependent operator distance
+`stateDepDistSq`. -/
+def multiplicativeDefect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℝ :=
+  stateDepDistSq (O u * O v) (O (u + v)) ρ
+
+/-- Pointwise form of the defect identity: for binary observables the squared
+defect of `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}` is `2 - 2 Re Tr(O^v O^u O^{v+u} ρ)`.  The
+expansion of `(O^u O^v - O^{u+v})^† (O^u O^v - O^{u+v})` produces the two
+triple products `O^v O^u O^{u+v}` and `O^{u+v} O^u O^v`; the second is the
+adjoint of the first, so their traces against `ρ` are complex conjugates with
+equal real parts.  This is the calculation behind display (3) of
+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`, applied to the products of the
+family. -/
+theorem multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
+    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
+    (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
+    multiplicativeDefect O ρ u v =
+      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (v + u) * ρ)).re := by
+  have hu := hO u
+  have hv := hO v
+  have huv := hO (u + v)
+  have hdiff :
+      (O u * O v - O (u + v))ᴴ * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
+        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) - O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
+    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq,
+      huv.1.eq]
+    calc
+      (O v * O u - O (u + v)) * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
+          O v * (O u * O u) * O v - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
+            O (u + v) * O u * O v + O (u + v) * O (u + v) := by
+        noncomm_ring
+      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
+            O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
+        rw [hu.2, Matrix.mul_one, hv.2, huv.2]
+        module
+  have hstar :
+      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
+        Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
+    calc
+      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
+          Matrix.trace ((O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)ᴴ) := by
+        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
+      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * (O v * O u * O (u + v))) := by
+        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq, huv.1.eq,
+          hρ.isHermitian.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc]
+      _ = Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
+        exact Matrix.trace_mul_comm _ _
+  have hcross :
+      (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)).re =
+        (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ)).re := by
+    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
+    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
+  unfold multiplicativeDefect stateDepDistSq
+  rw [hdiff]
+  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
+  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
+  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
+  rw [hcross, add_comm v u]
+  ring
+
+/-- The average multiplicative defect over a uniformly random pair equals
+`2 - 2 * (two-query correlation)`.  The pointwise identity
+`multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` produces the correlation
+summand with the two variables in reversed order; since the pair is uniform,
+exchanging the two coordinates leaves the average unchanged.  This is the
+relation between the approximate-linearity hypothesis of the QPBT quotation
+(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`) and
+display (7) of Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`),
+in the operator-distance normalization of
+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
+theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
+    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1) :
+    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
+        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
+      2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
+  have hswap :
+      avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
+        (fun pair =>
+          (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) =
+        blrCorrelation O ρ := by
+    unfold blrCorrelation
+    refine (avgOver_uniform_equiv (Equiv.prodComm _ _) _).trans ?_
+    exact avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair => rfl)
+  calc
+    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
+        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
+        avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
+          (fun pair => 2 - 2 *
+            (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) :=
+      avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair =>
+        multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace
+          pair.1 pair.2)
+    _ = 2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
+      rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_mul, avgOver_uniform_const, hswap]
+
+/-- The operator-valued BLR bound: under the correlation hypothesis of
+`exists_exactly_linear_observables`, the average squared defect of `O^u O^v`
+from `O^{u+v}` is at most `2 * δ`.  This is the passage from display (7) of
+Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`) to the
+approximate-linearity relation of the QPBT quotation
+(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`); the
+constant `2` is the operator-distance normalization recorded in
+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
+theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error {t : ℕ}
+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
+    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
+    (δ : ℝ) (hcorrelation : 1 - δ ≤ blrCorrelation O ρ) :
+    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
+        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) ≤ 2 * δ := by
+  rw [avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace]
+  linarith
+
+/-! ## The cubic Fourier identity -/
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier computations in the
+proof of Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick
+(`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096-1112`): a twisted form of the
+matrix-valued Parseval identity in which only the first factor is expanded
+through its Fourier coefficients.  Taking `a = 0` recovers Parseval. -/
+private theorem sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul {t : ℕ}
